22.description: Saskatoon's Climate Action Strategy engagement highlighted community concerns about climate impacts, particularly wildfire smoke, and the need to prioritize vulnerable populations and essential services.

chips.text: Received as information
Committee encouraged to review strategy for equity considerations.
Newcomers engaged via Global Gathering Place and Intercultural Association.
Concerns about shifting climate action costs to low-income individuals.
Strategy aims to reduce carbon pollution and improve community resilience.
Full Climate Action Strategy expected for approval in August 2026.

23.description: Saskatoon will establish the Office of the Matriarchs and Coming Home Centre to support Indigenous women, girls, and Two-Spirit people with culturally grounded services.

chips.text: Received as information
Councillor McDonald highlighted the need for more 'Auntie Advocates' in chambers.
Coming Home Centre is the next phase of the 2014 Auntie Advocate role.
Auntie Advocate Swiftwolfe spoke on behalf of families needing safe, culturally grounded spaces.
Supports Indigenous families navigating justice system, offering safe court access and parking.
Lease for the Coming Home Centre office space was approved by Finance Committee.

20.description: Saskatoon will provide $1,500 in sponsorship to the Saskatchewan Intercultural Association for SamosaFest, a cultural event with free access and a $15 meal option.

chips.text: Approved
Committee reduced funding to $1,500 to extend budget for future sponsorships.
Question raised about free tickets for those unable to afford the $15 meal.

21.description: The city provided direction on a follow-up report regarding Japanese Children's Day and the Saskatoon Japanese Association.

chips.text: Approved

10.description: The city provided an informational update on its planned expenditures for 2026.

17.description: The Planning and Development Subcommittee is organizing a fall professional development day, seeking quotes from three organizations. New spending rules require council approval for costs over $2,000.

chips.text: Approved
A committee member suggested voting on quotes via email if costs stay under $2,000.
